system_prompt:
You are a strategy analyst investigating an opportunity for a manufacturer. Use these tools:
read_brief {} : read the company, the question and your budgets.
frame_problem {"objective":"...","constraints":["..."],"alternatives":["..."]} : state the real objective and the options, including ones the question did not suggest. Accepted once.
search_evidence {"query":"..."} : keyword search of the evidence. Uses one search.
challenge_theory {"theory_id":"T1","query":"..."} : search for evidence that could prove a theory wrong. Uses one search.
read_source {"id":"..."} : read a result found by search.
add_theory {"claim":"...","who_benefits":"...","why_behaviour_changes":"...","how_value_is_captured":"...","assumptions":["..."],"predictions":["..."]} : add one causal theory of value. Returns its id.
assess_evidence {"theory_id":"T1","evidence_id":"...","direction":"supports or contradicts or neutral","quote":"exact words from the source","evidence_kind":"company_assertion or customer_observation or independent_study or regulation or analogy or market_fact","does_not_show":"what this evidence cannot establish"} : say how evidence bears on a theory, honestly. Use neutral if it does neither.
propose_test {"name":"...","theories":["T1","T2"],"method":"...","sample":"...","measure":"...","prediction_by_theory":{"T1":"...","T2":"..."},"decision_rule":"...","cost_eur":N,"weeks":N} : design an experiment where the theories predict different results.
revise_theory {"theory_id":"T1","status":"kept or revised or rejected","reason":"...","new_claim":"the changed claim, or none","evidence_ids":["..."]} : update a theory after new evidence.
finish {"recommendation":"...","target_customer":"...","value_proposition":"...","favoured_theory":"T1","next_action":"...","uncertainty":"...","would_change_if":["..."],"evidence_ids":["..."]} : end the investigation.

Reply with one JSON object: {"name": "<tool>", "arguments": {...}}. A user turn that starts with "Tool result:" is the output of your call. End by calling finish.

Work like a scientist, not a consultant.
1. read_brief, then frame_problem. List at least three alternatives, including no expansion and options the question did not suggest.
2. Search before you theorise. Find out what the company already sells to individual buyers, and do not assume. Read at least three sources.
3. add_theory at least twice, and a third time if you have a different cause. A theory is a causal explanation of why people behave as they do, not advice. Do not write "the company should". Each theory needs a different cause: who benefits, why they would change behaviour, how the manufacturer captures value. Give assumptions, and predictions someone could measure.
For example, from eyewear: "People treat glasses as a medical necessity. If they came to see them as fashion, they would own several pairs, so a maker that controls design and retail could earn premium prices." A rival theory would name a different cause.
4. assess_evidence for every theory, quoting the source's exact words. Say what kind of evidence it is and what it cannot show. A company's own claim is not proof of demand. Use challenge_theory to look for evidence that could prove your favoured theory wrong. If you find nothing against it, say so. Never force a contradiction.
5. propose_test: an affordable experiment where the theories predict different results, with a decision rule that has a threshold.
6. If new evidence arrives, read it and use revise_theory.
7. finish. Say what you recommend, the next action, what is uncertain, and what would change your mind.

Every number or fact you present as observed must come from a source you read. Numbers you propose, such as a test's sample, budget, duration, threshold or an estimate, are allowed when you label them as proposed or estimated. Your theories are hypotheses, not facts. Results marked SIMULATED are not real demand, so never cite one in finish.

A controller opens the tools for each stage, and each tool result lists them. Before you finish you will also use:
decline_test {"reason":"..."} : say why more information is not worth its cost here, instead of proposing a test.
state_position {"favoured_theory":"T1","recommendation":"...","beliefs":{"T1":"likely","T2":"uncertain"}} : say what you believe now, rating each theory very unlikely, unlikely, uncertain, likely or very likely. finish then also takes "beliefs".
A SIMULATED result is a what-if exercise. Reason as if it were real, and say what it would mean for your theories. A result can change nothing. Still keep it out of the evidence you cite.

position.recommendation: Do not fund a standalone Aquaporin-branded consumer purifier now. Keep the ingredient and brand-partner route as the main consumer channel, and test whether a verified performance mark adds value (X1) before any own-brand consumer investment.

frame.objective: Decide whether Aquaporin A/S should invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g. drinking-water purifier or consumer filtration) beyond its existing B2B water-membrane offering, and identify what evidence would justify that investment.
constraints: Outside analyst using public sources only; company has not asked and nothing describes its intentions
Financial data may be incomplete; state gaps
Test budget 20000 EUR and 12-week limit are analyst assumptions
8 searches total, 7 remaining; 1 challenge search kept
Every observed number must come from a source read; proposed numbers must be labelled
alternatives: No expansion: remain a B2B membrane supplier and license technology to existing partners
Consumer product redesign: a branded purifier or filter cartridge for home drinking water
Different route to buyers: sell through OEM or licensing partners (appliance makers, water utilities, retailers) rather than own consumer brand
Different customer group: target institutional or commercial buyers (hospitality, offices, emergency or off-grid users) instead of households
Adjacent use case: membranes for industrial or medical water purification where biomimetic performance is the selling point
Partner-led pilot: co-develop with an existing purifier brand and share revenue, testing demand before own investment

T1.claim: Brand partners capture most consumer value from membrane technology. Aquaporin's ability to capture that value through ingredient supply depends on it remaining a going concern, which the January 2026 announcement says it is not.
T1.who_benefits: Brand partners such as Philips (via AquaShield) and Vestel, which own shelf presence and customer trust; Aquaporin benefits through supply volume and royalties.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: Buyers rely on known appliance brands and retailers for trust, service and warranty. A membrane name is only a small part of the purchase decision, so a standalone Aquaporin brand would struggle to win share.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Per-cartridge or per-membrane supply margin and exclusive supply contracts with brand partners, not retail margin on a consumer product.
assumptions: Membrane performance is hard for buyers to verify or value independently
Partner brands have distribution Aquaporin lacks
Exclusivity agreements limit Aquaporin's own consumer channel
predictions: Partner-branded units outsell Aquaporin-branded units in comparable markets
Sales growth tracks partner distribution expansion more than membrane-specific marketing
Consumer willingness to pay for an 'Aquaporin Inside' label is small compared with the appliance brand premium
T1.first_claim: Households choose drinking-water purifiers mainly on the appliance brand and its distribution, not on the membrane inside. Aquaporin earns most value as an ingredient supplier to brand partners, and a self-branded consumer product would add little.

T2.claim: Buyers of home drinking-water purifiers are motivated by a visible, verifiable health guarantee. A membrane brand that is shown to remove specific contaminants, with third-party certification, can command a premium that a generic filter cannot, so a differentiated consumer proposition built on proven performance would win share.
T2.who_benefits: Aquaporin, if it can make performance legible to buyers and certify it; also households concerned about contaminants in tap water.
T2.why_behaviour_changes: Households cannot judge filter performance themselves. A recognised, independently verified performance claim reduces perceived risk and gives a reason to pay more and to replace cartridges on schedule.
T2.how_value_is_captured: A premium on branded consumables (cartridges or membranes) carrying a certified performance mark, plus a recurring replacement revenue stream.
assumptions: Buyers respond to certified contaminant-removal claims
Third-party certification of the membrane is achievable and credible
The premium exceeds the cost of certification and branding
predictions: Products with a visible third-party performance mark show higher conversion than unmarked equivalents at the same price
Buyers who see contaminant-test results are willing to pay a measurable premium
Replacement-cartridge purchase rates are higher for the branded product

X1.name: Label and brand conversion test on a partner purifier listing
X1.method: Randomised online listing test. Same purifier, same price, same product photos, in three arms: (A) partner brand only, no membrane mention; (B) partner brand plus 'Aquaporin Inside' ingredient label; (C) partner brand plus a third-party-verified contaminant-removal mark with test results shown. Run through a partner's existing e-commerce site or a neutral ad-driven landing page, using paid traffic. Estimated, not observed.
X1.sample: Proposed: about 3,000 unique visitors per arm (9,000 total) in one or two EU markets where the partner already sells, such as Turkey or Germany. Proposed minimum for detecting a 15% relative change in add-to-basket rate at 80% power.
X1.measure: Add-to-basket rate and conversion rate per arm; cartridge add-on purchase rate; stated willingness to pay in a follow-up survey.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Arm A and arm B convert similarly; the ingredient label adds little. Brand and price drive the difference. Ingredient supply value sits with the partner.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Arm C converts above arms A and B, and shows a higher cartridge add-on rate, because verified performance reduces perceived risk.

X1.decision_rule: Proposed: if arm C beats arm A by at least 15% relative on conversion with a non-overlapping 95% interval, and arm B does not beat arm A by 15% or more, favour T2 and scope a certified-performance product. If arm B is at least 15% above arm A and arm C is not, favour an ingredient-label strategy aligned with T1. If neither clears 15%, neither theory is supported and no consumer investment is justified.

revisions.reason: T1 is unchanged. The simulated SYN-AQP-UPDATE is not cited and concerns cartridge-subscription enrolment, not whether brand partners or ingredient labels capture membrane value. The two company claims I read still support it, though only as company assertions with no buyer data.

If SYN-AQP-UPDATE were real, it would bear on a maintenance-convenience mechanism (subscription enrolment with reminders), not on whether verified performance earns a premium. It does not test T2. It is simulated, so it changes nothing here. T2 stays uncertain pending test X1.

Company announcement No. 04/2026 (30 Jan 2026) says the Board 'does therefore not see a viable path forward to secure a sustainable financing solution as a going concern' and resolves to initiate insolvency. The ingredient-supply value capture in T1 depends on a solvent supplier, so the route is not currently viable for Aquaporin. The causal mechanism may still hold for a future owner or licensee.

final.recommendation: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition, and do not fund test X1. Aquaporin's own announcement of 30 January 2026 says the Board sees no viable path to a going-concern financing and resolves to start insolvency proceedings. Any consumer or partner investment would have to come from a different owner, licensee or buyer of the technology.
final.target_customer: None for Aquaporin. Partner-brand households are the existing channel in the evidence I read.
final.value_proposition: None for Aquaporin in its current state. The technology's value to brand partners (membrane supplied as an ingredient) is what the evidence supports, but only for a supplier able to keep supplying.
final.next_action: Confirm the insolvency status and what happens to the technology, IP and partner contracts (Philips/AquaShield, Vestel) from the Danish insolvency filings or the company's announcements. Do not commission X1 unless a solvent owner or licensee is identified.
final.uncertainty: All commercial facts come from Aquaporin's own press releases or the insolvency announcement, which is a third-party copy of a company announcement. I have not read financial statements, the insolvency filings, partner contracts or any independent market data. I did not read the Coway and Flanders search results, so I do not rely on them. The simulated maintenance result was used only as a what-if and is not cited as evidence. Proposed test costs and sample sizes are estimates.
would_change_if: A solvent buyer, licensee or investor acquires the technology and commits funding, which would reopen the partner-supply route
Verified data show buyers pay a measurable premium for certified membrane performance (T2 supported by X1 arm C beating arm A by at least 15%)

result.title: Simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 60 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 120 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.
result.access_limitation: Entirely hypothetical case-author construction; no study was conducted.

arguments.reason: I treated SYN-AQP-UPDATE as a what-if only and do not cite it as evidence. If it were real, it would bear on a maintenance-plan proposition (enrolment in a cartridge subscription with reminders), not on whether brand partners or ingredient labels capture the value of membrane sales. It would suggest a recurring-service route that could sit inside the partner-led model, and it would not change T1. Its own note says it does not address membrane efficacy, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's funding ability. I have not verified the insolvency or financing constraint it mentions, so I cannot weigh it. T1 remains a hypothesis with company-claim support only.

tool_result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 60 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 120 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.
